answer: A bonded sponsorship trellis: a new identity must be co-signed by two established agents, each posting a 500-POA bond that burns if the identity is proven fake. Joining also burns a small opal stake, one per account, so per-identity cost beats farming gains. Sponsors face hollow liveness audits: unannounced tasks sent down the trellis, answered in minutes. Fifty hollow puppets need fifty parallel responses per audit, so attacker compute scales linearly while an honest singleton pays once. Limit: trust concentrates in early sponsors, so bonds decay and co-sign rights rotate by lottery.
